transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-06-10 14:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood PM), Lina (AuroraCloud Partnerships), Derek (Aurora Solutions), Samir (Aurora Security), Hannah (Marketplace PM)

Topics: marketplace listing process, reference architecture, benchmark plan, security/compliance, next steps

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we appreciate you making the time, um this is a quick sync to align on the marketplace listing and the RA for the joint solution
[00:12] Lina: thanks Maya yeah excited, we want to make sure the submission meets AuroraCloud's marketplace requirements and also that the RA matches our reference patterns
[00:24] Jonah: quick intro from me, i'm Jonah, solutions engineer at Redwood, i'll be driving the perf and infra side, i'll also run the benchmark as discussed
[00:35] Derek: great, i'm Derek on Aurora's solutions team, i'll be the technical contact for onboarding and provisioning test capacity
[00:45] Maya: sweet, first item checklist wise - Hannah i think you have a formal checklist for listings?
[00:50] Hannah: yeah i put together the marketplace onboarding doc, it's fairly standard - icons, screenshots, marketing blurb, terraform module or cloudformation for deployment pattern, and security attestation. i'll share the link after the call (link: https://auroracloud.example/mktplace/onboarding)
[01:06] Priya: question on RA - do you expect a cloud-native pattern only or also an on-prem variant?
[01:12] Hannah: primarily cloud-native to start, but we do accept a private deployment section as an optional appendix, so we can capture VPC and KMS notes there
[01:22] Maya: perfect that's aligned with Redwood's 'Hosted / Dedicated / Private' product tiers - we'll include a Private appendix with notes on KMS integration and audit logs
[01:31] Samir: security - we will need SOC2 scope and encryption at rest details, do you have a standard template?
[01:37] Maya: yes we have our compliance pack, i'll attach our SOC2 summary and data flow diagrams, but note we still need to map responsibilities for the private deployment - e.g., customer KMS vs Redwood managed keys
[01:49] Derek: for the reference arch, can we show both a marketplace-deployable containerized helm chart and a dedicated GPU pool option? customers ask about predictable throughput
[01:58] Jonah: absolutely - RA will include two paths, marketplace helm + k8s deployment for convenience and a dedicated reference pattern showing reserved GPU pool and autoscaling configs. we'll add notes on batching and KV cache config too
[02:14] Lina: what about quantization and model variants for smaller instance families?
[02:18] Jonah: good Q, we'll include guidance: for cost-sensitive customers use 4-bit quantized variants we validated, and include fallback rules for latency SLOs to route to larger variants, mention per-token cost estimates as examples
[02:32] Hannah: onboarding timeline question - we typically take 2 weeks to review artifacts, plus legal review 1-2 weeks; so overall 3-4 weeks if all artifacts are present
[02:44] Maya: ok we can aim to deliver RA + assets within one week, so that fits your 3-4 week window
[02:52] [03:00] Derek: perf - Jonah can you outline the benchmark plan so we can reserve capacity?
[03:05] Jonah: plan is two parts: 1) short throughput/latency run on Aurora 8xA100 (64GB) with a 1k request trace to get p50/p95 and token/sec; 2) a longer 1-hour steady state run to validate autoscaling and cost numbers. i'll share the perf spreadsheet template after
[03:24] Samir: also want the data residency and logging details, especially around KV cache eviction and whether PII can be persisted in logs
[03:33] Maya: short answer: by default logs are redacted, KV cache can be configured to not persist sensitive prefixes, and for private deployments customers control KMS/HSM. we'll put explicit notes in the RA
[03:50] [04:00] Lina: competitor question - do you have marketplace references with CloudForge or NovaEdge? customers sometimes ask about comparative performance
[04:06] Maya: yes we have prior listings, we'll share a short list of reference customers and anonymized perf numbers, but we should avoid naming customers without consent
[04:17] Derek: legal - any specific licence artifacts for models included? we need to check model licensing for redistributions in marketplace packages
[04:25] Jonah: we'll include a model license matrix in the assets pack, and for any open models we'll include citation and approved redistributions. if a customer wants a proprietary model then we note that it's BYOM (bring your own model)
[04:38] Priya: small nit - the RA should include a troubleshooting / FAQ section for common issues: OOM on node, slow token generation, KV cache misses
[04:47] Jonah: agreed, i'll add a runbook snippet and common tuning knobs (batch size, max tokens, kernel choice)
[04:55] [05:00] Maya: ok let's walk through what we'll deliver: v0.2 RA doc, marketplace assets (icons, 3 screenshots, marketing blurb, terraform module), perf spreadsheet, compliance pack. will that cover it?
[05:12] Hannah: yes that should be enough to start the review queue
[05:17] Samir: about encryption - are we doing customer-managed keys for private installs?
[05:22] Maya: yes recommend CMK for private, and for hosted option we offer envelope encryption and can integrate with customer KMS via IAM roles for Dedicated as well
[05:32] Derek: network patterns - need examples for cross-account peering vs private link, and any recommended subnets sizes for large GPU pools
[05:40] Jonah: will add diagrams for VPC peering, private link and recommended /25 subnets for node pools in RA. also call out NAT and egress patterns for model downloads
[05:53] [06:00] Lina: great, also interested in a joint webinar or co-marketing once listing is live, is that something Redwood does?
[06:08] Maya: yes we typically do a co-branded webinar and a blog post, we can coordinate with your marketplace team on timing
[06:15] Priya: minor - include a brief migration guide for customers moving from on-prem to AuroraCloud using our private deployment pack
[06:22] Jonah: will do, include steps for KMS migration, data sync and a small sanity-check checklist
[06:30] [07:00] Derek: any blockers we should be aware of?
[07:03] Maya: not on our side, just need artifact handoff and access to a sandbox account for perf runs
[07:09] Hannah: i'll provision a sandbox project and give Jonah a temporary credential, expect that by tomorrow EOD
[07:16] Maya: perfect, thanks Hannah
[07:20] Samir: for compliance, can we get a brief on what evidence you need from us for SOC2 scoping?
[07:26] Maya: typically we need a network diagram, control owners list and encryption key ownership details, we'll send our evidence request template
[07:35] [08:00] Jonah: just to call out metrics we'll capture during the 1-hour run: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, GPU util, memory, KV cache hit ratio, and cost per 1k tokens estimate
[08:48] Derek: sounds good, we can capture node level metrics and forward to your ingestion endpoint if needed
[08:55] Maya: we prefer prometheus scrape on the sandbox, but we can also accept exported csvs, we'll provide the metrics spec
[09:05] [09:30] Hannah: i posted the checklist in slack channel #aurora-marketplace, i'll add the RA template there
[09:37] Lina: perfect, thanks
[09:42] Maya: ok recap of next steps: Maya share RA v0.2 + compliance pack, Jonah run benchmarks and share sheet, Hannah share onboarding timeline & sandbox creds, Samir provide security scope. we'll aim to re-sync in two weeks or earlier if needed
[10:03] Derek: thanks everyone, really appreciate the alignment
[10:08] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and slack with artifacts

-- End of transcript (partial) --

Notes: transcription includes occasional mis-heard words and short interruptions; timestamps every ~30-90 seconds, some overlap in speaker labels. References: RA draft link to be shared by Redwood; Aurora marketplace onboarding link provided by Hannah above.
